_meta.notes: Slot contracts for build_site.py. Types: text (plain), inline (**bold**, *italic*, [label](url)), rich (paragraphs, - lists, ### subheads, > quotes), link {label, href}, image {src, alt}, enum, bool, icon, id, email, url, number, list, object. required=true stops the build with a message naming the block and slot. max is a soft character limit that only warns. Run: python3 scripts/build_site.py blocks [NAME]

id.desc: Anchor for links, like #pricing. Defaults to the block type.

nav_label.desc: Puts this section in the automatic top menu under this label.

tone.desc: Background band. auto alternates plain and tinted bands down the page.

site.desc: Top level of site.json. Only name and one page of blocks are required.

name.desc: Business or site name. Used in the menu, page titles, footer and structured data.

tagline.desc: One line after the name in the home page title, e.g. 'Halden & Co: operations for small teams'.

url.desc: Final address, e.g. https://halden.co.uk. Turns on canonical links, sitemap and share tags. Leave it out until the address is known, then rebuild.

lang.desc: Language code (en, fr, nl, de...). Non-English sites should also set ui.

preset.desc: Design preset name. Run: python3 scripts/build_site.py presets

tokens.desc: Overrides on the preset: colors {accent, bg, ...}, radius {sm, md, lg}, fonts {heading, body}, style {...}, container, space_unit. Run: python3 scripts/build_site.py tokens PRESET

fonts.desc: google loads the preset fonts from Google Fonts; system uses only fonts already on the visitor's device (no external requests, faster, more private).

dark_mode.desc: Follow the visitor's dark mode when the preset has a dark palette.

nav.desc: Menu links. Leave out to build the menu from blocks and pages that have nav_label. '#id' links point at the home page from any page.

nav_cta.desc: One highlighted button at the end of the menu.

nav_sticky.desc: Keep the menu at the top while scrolling.

logo.desc: Logo image used instead of the text name in the menu. alt should be the business name.

legal.desc: Small print such as a company number.

business.desc: Facts for search engines (structured data). Only what is true.

type.desc: Organization, LocalBusiness or a schema.org subtype such as Restaurant, Dentist, LegalService, ProfessionalService.

country.desc: Two letter code such as GB or BE.

og_image.desc: Share image: a file inside public/ (1200x630 works best) or an https URL.

public.desc: Folder of images and files copied as-is into the site. Default: public/ next to site.json.

custom_css.desc: Path to a .css file, or CSS text, appended after the base styles. Use var(--accent) style variables, never raw colors.

noindex.desc: Ask search engines to skip the site (drafts). Remove before launch.

year.desc: Year in the footer copyright. Default: the current year.

ui.desc: Text the builder adds itself (skip link, menu label, form labels, 404 page). Set these for any language other than English.

csp.desc: false turns off the Content-Security-Policy header. An object adds sources, e.g. {"frame-src": ["https://www.youtube.com"]}.

path.desc: '/' for the home page, '/about' for another page.

title.desc: Browser and search title. Default: built from the hero headline and site name.

nav_label.desc: Puts the page in the automatic menu.

blocks.desc: Sections in order. The first must be a hero.

pages.desc: The pages. Or give blocks directly for a one page site.

blocks.desc: Shortcut for a one page site: the sections of the home page.

nav.desc: Menu bar with logo or name, links and one optional button. Built for you from site.nav, site.nav_cta, site.logo and site.nav_sticky.

hero.desc: Opening screen with the page's only h1. Text only, or split with an image when image is set. compact:true makes a slim page header for inner pages.

headline.desc: The h1. What you do and for whom, in plain words.

subhead.desc: One or two sentences that finish the thought.

cta.desc: The single action you want (book, buy, sign up).

note.desc: Reassurance under the buttons, e.g. 'Free to try. No card.'

image.desc: Turns on the split layout. Use only a real photo or illustration the owner supplied.

compact.desc: Slim page header for inner pages.

align.desc: Text alignment. Default comes from the preset.

example.headline: Your team is busy. Your systems should not be.
example.subhead: We set up scheduling, invoicing and handover, then run the first quarter with you.

proof-bar.desc: Slim strip of proof: client names as text (or small logos), or two to four short facts. Only real ones.

image.desc: Optional logo file. Without it the name is set as a wordmark.

features.desc: Two to nine things you offer or reasons to choose you. variant rows reads like a contents list (best for 3 to 5 longer items), cards suits 4 to 9 short ones, plain is the quietest.

columns.desc: Cards and plain only. Default depends on the item count.

icon.desc: Optional. One of the sprite icons; skip it unless it means something.

example.title: Three jobs we take off your desk

items.title: Scheduling that holds
items.text: One shared calendar, clear rules for changes.

items.title: Invoicing that gets paid
items.text: Templates, reminders and a weekly check.

items.title: Handover that sticks
items.text: Written routines your team can follow without us.

split.desc: Text beside an image, a fact panel, or alone. For a story, an approach or a single strong argument. reverse:true swaps the sides.

body.desc: Paragraphs. Blank line between them; '- ' for a list; '### ' for a small heading.

points.desc: Short ticked lines under the text.

image.desc: Photo or illustration the owner supplied.

panel.desc: A big fact shown instead of an image.

example.title: We stay until it runs without us
example.body:
Most advice ends with a document.

Ours ends with a team that no longer needs us.

steps.desc: A numbered process of two to six steps.

items.title: Listen
items.text: A week of calls and a written diagnosis.

items.title: Build
items.text: We set up the routines that matter most.

items.title: Run
items.text: We run them with you and adjust.

testimonials.desc: Real quotes from real customers. One quote is set large; two to six become a grid. Never invent them: skip the block when there are none.

image.desc: Optional portrait. Without it initials are shown.

items.quote: They found two days a week we did not know we were losing.
items.name: Priya Nair

pricing.desc: One to three plans. Use only prices the owner confirmed. featured:true highlights one plan.

badge.desc: Label on the featured plan. Default: ui.popular.

note.desc: Small print under the plans (taxes, terms).

faq.desc: Two to twelve questions that stop people buying. Answers can hold links and short lists.

items.q: Do you work with tiny teams?
items.a: Yes. Most clients have between two and twelve people.
Half at the start, half at handover.

stats.desc: Two to four big numbers with labels. Only true, checkable numbers the owner gave you.

cta.desc: Full-width closing call to action in the accent color. One button, maybe a quieter second.

example.title: Tell us what is slowing you down

contact.desc: How to reach you. Without form_action it shows an email button (a static site cannot receive forms by itself). With form_action (a form service the owner signs up to, such as Formspree) it shows a real form.

email.desc: Shown and used for the mail button.

button.desc: Button label. Default: ui.send or ui.email_us.

subject.desc: Subject line for the mail button.

form_action.desc: https:// endpoint of a form service. Public, not a secret.

text.desc: Plain reading page section: about text, policies, long explanations. width narrow keeps lines readable.

example.title: Our story
example.body:
Halden & Co began in 2019.

We write things down.

footer.desc: Footer with name, short text, optional link columns, social links and copyright. Built for you from site.footer and site.business.
